Based on the chest X-ray findings of the two cases, which statement accurately describes the progression and characteristics of pulmonary findings in Case 2 during hospitalization?

A) The initial chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral consolidations, which completely resolve by the time of hospital discharge.
B) The initial chest X-ray shows bilateral peripheral consolidations that improve with remaining atelectatic streaks in the right basal zone by discharge.
C) The initial chest X-ray shows bilateral peripheral consolidations, and there is complete resolution with no remaining findings by the time of discharge.
D) The initial chest X-ray shows bilateral peripheral consolidations, which improve to reveal thin atelectatic streaks in the left basal zone by discharge.
E) The initial chest X-ray shows right perihilar consolidation, which progresses to bilateral pleural effusion by discharge.
F) The initial chest X-ray shows bilateral peripheral consolidations, which deteriorate over time leading to worsened opacities by discharge.
